response.sql:
WITH per_patient AS (
  SELECT ID, AVG(1.0 * HGB / HCT) AS avg_ratio
  FROM Laboratory
  WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL AND HCT IS NOT NULL AND HCT <> 0
  GROUP BY ID
), overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS overall_avg
  FROM per_patient
), first_group AS (
  SELECT p.ID, p.avg_ratio, o.overall_avg,
         p.avg_ratio - o.overall_avg AS above_overall
  FROM per_patient p CROSS JOIN overall o
  WHERE p.avg_ratio > o.overall_avg
), second_avg AS (
  SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS group_avg
  FROM first_group
), final_group AS (
  SELECT f.avg_ratio, f.above_overall,
         f.avg_ratio - s.group_avg AS above_second
  FROM first_group f CROSS JOIN second_avg s
  WHERE f.avg_ratio > s.group_avg
)
SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS average_ratio,
       AVG(above_overall) AS average_amount_above_overall,
       AVG(above_second) AS average_amount_above_second
FROM final_group;

assumptions.assumption: The overall and second-stage averages are unweighted averages of patient-level mean ratios; each eligible patient contributes equally. A per-test ratio is computable when HGB and HCT are non-NULL and HCT is nonzero.
